standard_prerequisites.name: Homeomorphism of a bijective map of profinite spaces
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Topology, the lemma that a continuous bijection from a profinite space to a compact Hausdorff space is a homeomorphism

standard_prerequisites.name: The localization construction and faithfulness of local isomorphisms
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the localization construction attached to a locally closed subscheme and the lemma that a local isomorphism which is a homeomorphism on spaces is an isomorphism
standard_prerequisites.use: Supply the ring B = (A_w)_T^tilde and the conclusion that A/I -> B/IB is an isomorphism.

core_obligations: Cut out the subset (proof lines 1019-1024): let A -> A_w be the w-localization with closed point set Z and let T be the inverse image of the closed subset V(I) in Z; then T -> V(I) is a homeomorphism because both are profinite and the map is a continuous bijection.
Build the localization (proof lines 1024-1026): set B equal to the localization (A_w)_T^tilde; it is clear that B is w-local and that its set of closed points is V(IB).

Conclude the isomorphism (proof lines 1026-1030): the induced ring map A/I -> B/IB is ind-Zariski and induces a homeomorphism on the underlying spaces, hence it is an isomorphism by the faithfulness statement for local isomorphisms, which gives A/I = B/IB as required.
proof_roadmap: Take the inverse image of the profinite closed subset in the closed points of the w-localization.
Localize the w-localization along that subset and read off w-locality and the closed points.
Show that the map on the quotients is a local isomorphism and a homeomorphism, hence an isomorphism.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a ring A and a closed subset V(I) of its spectrum which is profinite, there is an ind-Zariski ring map A -> B with Spec(B) w-local, closed point set V(IB) and A/I isomorphic to B/IB (statement lines 1011-1017). The proof (proof lines 1019-1031) takes the inverse image of V(I) in the closed points of the w-localization, localizes along it, and concludes the isomorphism from faithfulness of local isomorphisms. H2: a three-step construction with three inputs, written out in full.
